requirement:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

story.summary: Every source-generator template (object formatter, string-key formatter, enum formatter, union formatter, the generated resolver and the composite resolver) now writes `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on the generated class. The resolver templates also put it on their nested helper classes. Each attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. A one-character fix in TransformUtilities makes the opening brace of a constrained nesting type end with a newline, so the new `#if` lands at the start of a line. About 222 expected-output snapshots were regenerated, a new test class checks the generated text, and the README documents the behaviour.
story.why: The issue asks for all generated MessagePack code to carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage so it stops skewing coverage numbers. No setting was added, which the issue says is acceptable.
touches_beyond_requirement: TransformUtilities.cs line 58 changes the brace emitted after a constrained nesting type from "{" to "{\r\n". This is needed so the preprocessor directive starts a line, but it also changes the layout of existing generated output (the +4/-1 and +5/-1 snapshot shapes).
Per-target `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard: a product decision the issue did not ask for.
README paragraph documenting the behaviour and the guard.
story.confidence_overview: High that each template now emits the guarded attribute at the intended places; the .tt and .cs pairs match line for line. Medium on the snapshots: only 2 of 222 were visible, and S2 flags 7 distinct shapes, which the brace-newline change plausibly explains. Low confidence that the guard is justified. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.x, so those consumers get no exclusion and the README states a wrong reason. The new tests check text per generated file, not per type. They do not compile the output and may not exercise the enum or composite templates.

claims.text: The object (integer-key) formatter template emits the guarded ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute immediately before `internal sealed class <Formatter>`. The .tt and compiled .cs agree.
claims.requirement_quote: I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

breaker.reason: FormatterTemplate.tt (lines 14-16) and FormatterTemplate.cs (line 33) wrap [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, so the requirement is only partly met. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute (parameterless constructor on classes) has been available in .NET Framework since 4.0 (System.dll) and in .NET Standard since 2.0 (netstandard.dll), so this guard needlessly strips the attribute for all netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers.

claims.text: When a nesting type has generic constraints, EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces now writes "{\r\n" instead of "{". The following `#if` directive therefore starts on its own line, which C# requires for preprocessor directives. Before, the string-key and union templates put the class declaration on the same line as the brace.

breaker.reason: Checked TransformUtilities.cs line 58, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs line 37, and UnionTemplate.cs line 30. Previously, when anyConstraints was true, EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces wrote an opening brace with no newline while StringKeyFormatterTemplate and UnionTemplate did not emit a leading newline before the class declaration, which would have put #if on the same line as the brace (CS1040). The GenericDataTypeWithPrivateMember snapshot line counts (+5/-1 and +4/-0) corroborate this.

claims.text: Helper RunGeneratorAsync builds a C# compilation with default framework and MessagePack references and runs MessagePackGenerator through a generator driver. It returns each generated tree's path and text, and discards diagnostics without compiling the output. CountOccurrences counts non-overlapping ordinal matches.

breaker.reason: Checked CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs lines 99-129: CountOccurrences (lines 99-110) counts non-overlapping StringComparison.Ordinal matches by advancing index by value.Length, and RunGeneratorAsync (lines 112-129) compiles against DefaultTargetFrameworkReferences plus ReferencesSet.MessagePack, runs MessagePackGenerator, discards out compilation and diagnostics on line 123 without compiling the generated trees, and returns path/text tuples.

claims.text: The test file header, usings, attribute and guard string constants, and fixture source define int-key, string-key, enum and union types plus a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]` partial class. No type in the fixture references the enum, and it has no composite resolver.

Claim C13 disputed: Although the sample snapshots match the templates at TypeWithAutoGeneratedFormatterFormatter.g.cs lines 12-14 and MessagePack.GeneratedMessagePackResolver.g.cs lines 12-14, 29-31, and 46-48, the emitted #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK guard strips [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+ despite the attribute being available there, so the quoted requirement is only partly met.

Claim C14 disputed: README.md line 1640 states that [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, which is factually incorrect (System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has been in System.dll since .NET Framework 4.0 and in netstandard.dll since .NET Standard 2.0), and omitting it on those targets only partly meets the requirement.

The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard, repeated in every template, drops the attribute for projects targeting netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists there (netstandard2.0, .NET Framework 4.0+), so the guard looks unnecessary. Those consumers, a large part of MessagePack's user base, keep getting skewed coverage, contrary to 'all generated code'.
The README states the attribute is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. That appears factually wrong and would mislead users about why their coverage is still skewed.

The test named AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage only checks that each generated file contains the attribute at least once. A file with several types where only one is decorated would pass.

The `>= 5` threshold is met by the int-key, string-key, union-member and union formatters plus the resolver. It does not prove an enum formatter was generated, and the fixture's enum is not referenced by any member. The enum template and the composite resolver template are not exercised by the new tests.

Generator diagnostics and the updated compilation are discarded. The new tests never confirm that the generated code still compiles, for example with the directive placement. That relies on the existing snapshot tests.

Changing the brace output for constrained nesting types alters generated layout for every template using EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces, adding a blank line in the formatter and enum cases. This is cosmetic but is behind S2's 7 distinct snapshot shapes. Only 2 of the 222 snapshots could be inspected.

All six generator templates, CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs (lines 18-19), and README.md (line 1640) guard [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] with #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK on the mistaken assumption that ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not exist on those targets (likely confusing it with nullable analysis attributes added in netstandard2.1 or the Justification property added in .NET 5). Because the parameterless ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute on classes has existed since .NET Framework 4.0 and .NET Standard 2.0, consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework (such as net472/net48) needlessly get no code coverage exclusion on generated code, and README.md documents an untrue statement.

Assert.True(generated.Count >= 5) passes for the wrong reason: line 69 expects 5 files from 1 int-key formatter, 1 string-key formatter, 1 enum formatter, 1 union formatter, and 1 resolver, but MyEnum is unreferenced so no enum formatter is emitted, while MyUnionMember ([MessagePackObject]) silently supplies a second int-key formatter to reach 5. As a result, EnumTemplate (as well as CompositeResolverTemplate) is completely untested by CodeCoverageExclusionTests.
